questions.text:
Six students P, Q, R, S, T and U, with distinct heights, compare their heights and make the following observations.

Observation I: S is taller than R.
Observation II: Q is the shortest of all.
Observation III: U is taller than only one student.
Observation IV: T is taller than S but is not the tallest

The number of students that are taller than R is the same as the number of students shorter than ____________.
questions.solution:
From the observations: Q is shortest, U is second shortest, and T is taller than S but not tallest, so P is the tallest. R is shorter than S and above U.

Order (short [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] tall): Q, U, R, S, T, P.

Taller than R: S, T, P = 3. Shorter than S: R, U, Q = 3.

Answer: S

questions.text:
The number of units of a product sold in three different years and the respective net profits are presented in the figure above. The cost/unit in Year 3 was Re. 1, which was half the cost/unit in Year 2. The cost/unit in Year 3 was one-third of the cost/unit in Year 1. Taxes were paid on the selling price at 10%, 13%, and 15% respectively for the three years. Net profit is calculated as the difference between the selling price and teh sum of cost and taxes paid in that year.

The ratio of the selling price in Year 2 to the selling price in Year 3 is _________.
questions.solution:
Cost/unit: Year 3 = 1, Year 2 = 2.
Net profit = SP [latex]-[/latex] cost [latex]-[/latex] tax on SP = SP(1 [latex]-[/latex] t) [latex]-[/latex] cost.
- Year 2: 200 units, cost 400, profit 296, tax 13%: [latex]0.87\,SP=696\Rightarrow SP=800[/latex]
- Year 3: 300 units, cost 300, profit 210, tax 15%: [latex]0.85\,SP=510\Rightarrow SP=600[/latex]

Ratio = 800 : 600 = 4 : 3

Answer: 4 : 3

questions.text:
The number of students in three classes is in the ratio 3:13:6. If 18 students are added to each class, the ratio changes to 15:35:21.

The total number of students in all the three classes in the beginning was:
questions.solution:
Let the classes be 3k, 13k, 6k. After adding 18 to each:
[latex]\frac{3k+18}{13k+18}=\frac{15}{35}=\frac37\Rightarrow21k+126=39k+54\Rightarrow k=4[/latex]

Initial total = 22k = 88. (Check: 30 : 70 : 42 = 15 : 35 : 21 True)

Answer: 88

questions.text: A jigsaw puzzle has 2 pieces. One of the pieces is shown above. Which one of the given options for the missing piece when assembled will form a rectangle? The piece can be moved, rotated or flipped to assemble with the above piece.
questions.solution:
The given piece has a straight right edge and a jagged left edge with teeth of different lengths. The missing piece, rotated to sit next to it, must have teeth that exactly fill those gaps.

Only option A has the matching pattern of widths and depths, so together they form a rectangle.

Answer: A

questions.text:
Listening to music during exercise improves performance and reduces discomfort. Scientists researched whether listening to music while studying can help students learn better and the results were inconclusive. Students who needed external stimulation for studying fared worse while students who did not need any external stimulation benefited from music.

Which one of the following statements is the CORRECT inference of the above passage?
questions.solution:
The passage says music clearly helps physical exercise, but for studying the results were mixed: it helped some students and hurt others.

Answer: Clear positive effect on exercise; positive effect on learning only in some students
